## IO Pulse: Recast and Quarantined \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-pulse-recast-and-quarantined)\]

Following after the final IO LP, "IO Pulse", I took the chance to work with some of my favorite musicians from around the world on new versions of that last album: K Sabroso ([Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/artist/2LYvbnHReAOIyMeGM2IjhU?si=B2lW2dIJQR2vhjcStsJFpA)), ZITAN ([Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/artist/6DHq8DyGkCxrw4AJjNfGJt?si=klWJG5ffQ5OsUsBEJxbwrg)), Gaea Phoenix, Sp@rkle Jade (not to be confused with Geisha Punk Jade), IndustrialDeath, Maya Ava (not to be confused with Maya Shivaswami), and of course BMFD. Always BMFD. _You rock good brotha!_

To this day, K Sabroso's remix of "Trinity" remains my favorite and finds itself on nearly every playlist. ZITAN's remix of "Witching Wall" has spread far and wide, going viral on SoundCloud when it first launched. Then the three fates? The three fates woke the dead earth of the song, breathing new life into it and fanning the flames to wake the ash into fire.

I used similar symbolism from the original album art, but this time as a containment wall to hold in the burning world behind this barrier... as if the blood inside could truly ever be contained.

You can listen to and/or download the album [here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-pulse-recast-and-quarantined).

## The Last Memory of Laughter \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-last-memory-of-laughter)\]

_<font face="Times New Roman">The 8th and final chapter in the "IO" series, carrying the broken body of the Daughter of Sol to her tragic end. Good night, sweet Terra. Sleep well. There is no more laughter here. There is only a memory.</font>_

This is my favorite EP in the IO series... and, as all good things must come to an end, it marks the end of the entire series. This is also my favorite story in the IO series... forever marked by a field of forget-me-not flowers growing in the shadow of a twisted, blasted tower that overlooks a lake where a broken, metallic angel cradles the metal body of another in its arms.

All laughter has fled from this world. But one, just one of the main characters, still remembers one of the jokes of the old world. It's not a good joke, but it... it's a reason to laugh. It's a reason to _remember_ laughing... to remember moments _worth_ laughing in.

And on that note, the darkest and heaviest chapter of the IO story kicks off. On a suicide mission. It carries with it unlikely alliances, questionable choices, and a vision of what the dregs of humanity may one day become when the world has left the species behind. So you've been warned, traveler.

_Turn back... or continue the story [here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-last-memory-of-laughter)._

PS: Yes, yes the novella is really coming. I haven't forgotten.

## IO Pulse \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-pulse)\]

The 4th and final LP in the "IO" series. This is the earth element in the series -- dense, thick, and heavy; progressing from classical compositions into more and more electronic arenas. Every song is 3-minutes and 30-seconds, every song is 128bpm, and every song shares the same 4th beat. On this "pulse" the music grows and evolves through the closing EP of the series.

I'll end my words here, instead adding in the comments made by PK of Peppermill Records and King Deluxe:

_<font face="Times New Roman">Do you ever come out of a great festival experience with a theme song? The soundtrack to an epic weekend based on one pivotal moment? Many of you must be nodding your head. In fact, take a moment to think back and revel in nostalgia.</font>_

_<font face="Times New Roman">"The Witching Wall", the opener on San Jaya Prime’s new album IO Pulse, falls in the same category. Although it's opposite, as when I hear it I picture all the sites and sounds and sand of Black Rock City. And in this case, Jaya Prime actually did attend and perform. I was the one who never made it. Stuck in Canada.</font>_

_<font face="Times New Roman">I believe Jaya's most defining moments are still ahead of him, however there’s some true moments of brilliance here. It leaves me anticipating his next steps.</font>_

Listen to and/or download IO Pulse [here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-pulse).

**Extended Listening**:

If you liked "IO Pulse" then the fan-favorite of the series is easily "[IO Vapoura](io-vapoura)", or the newer 20-year anniversary edition of "[IO Limiters](io-limiters)" -- the very first LP in the IO series.

## The Shadows of Sunset \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-shadows-of-sunset)\]

For the third EP in the IO series, I collaborated with none other than my brother aychEff Zero himself; aka, "DJ Chad Is a DJ"; aka, "Stereoweary Workshop". From the infamous song "Chad's House" to the now-legendary "2TLXLI" (and a fan fav at our live shows), even with the opening symphonic electro version of "Blood and Oil", this EP kicks off and just doesn't let go. There's even the nZambi version of my award winning song "Escape from Hunahpu" (Peppermill Records, King Deluxe).

Much to my chagrin, I've never been able to pin down Zero long enough to get him on stage with us. SPEQTRA, who helped close out "Bonjour Bitches!", has stepped in for parts of 2TLXLI on stage, and even more famously we've had Dez murder the song in her own way (see, "[Warriors in Waiting](warriors-in-waiting-live-set)"). I've tried getting Zero up with us. At the moment, I'm thinking I'll either need a tranquilizer gun or a taser. I just haven't decided which one will do the least damage in order to have him stage-ready.

You can listen to the full anomalistic EP [here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-shadows-of-sunset).

Then you can find Zero's anomalistic podcast [here on Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/2nWZxLxgASjUbhYi2K0hKP?si=QNJsgsJJQ4SwHKNZ2TY7Fw).

## IO Teknika (in Four Movements) \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-teknika-in-four-movements)\]

Firstly, so much love and gratitude to my sister Gaea and Tricky Fish Photography for helping with the album art shots. Also, lottsa laughter about how many times that candle threatened to light everything on fire... starting with me!

In many ways, a production version of this album almost never happened. Near the end of 2006, after the death of Wolf Willie, I stood at a crossroads looking at two lives. I was homeless at the time, and I'd been working on at least two of these songs for a year already... even playing a live version of "Arizona Bay" with Tunzer in TAOS. I could stay homeless and focus only on music, building up my name amid the underground from festival to festival... or I could trade off the road for an office job and look into making a production version.

Being that I took that latter path, and it led to one of the best road trips in 2008, I'm happy to have chosen this way. But do I wonder about the other? About where I'd wind up on that other path? _You bet your ass I do!_ Maybe one day I'll meet up with the variant of me who took that path.

As the fire element in the IO series, much of this music came naturally to me.

Listen to and/or download _IO Teknika_ [here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/io-teknika-in-four-movements).

## The Smell of a Storm \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-smell-of-a-storm)\]

The fresh ozone of an electrical storm rolling in... the crisp frosty scent of an incoming hailstorm... and of course the bursting petrichor of the earth itself once the storm has passed. Almost exclusively for fans of 8bit Breaks, Chiptune, Atmospheric DnB, and glitch. Bleeps, bloops, whirs, and alotta snare.

I'll come right out and say that "The Smell of a Storm" is probably my least popular album. Jungle and DnB had their time, but it fell out of favor Stateside and in most parts of Europe. That doesn't mean the rest of the world doesn't love it, as Argentina college radio in fact prefers this EP along with "The Ash of a Thousand Suns" EP that preceded this (see below).

I'm working on a special project for those who in fact liked this EP, something I've been stirring around for more than a decade. When it's ready, you'll be the first to hear it.

Listen to and/or download the EP [here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-smell-of-a-storm).

## The Ash of a Thousand Suns \[[Free DL](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-ash-of-a-thousand-suns)\]

My very first EP in the IO series and a massive hit pretty much everywhere but the USA. The closing song "Kandela de Esperanza" has more than 80,000 plays ([SoundCloud](https://soundcloud.com/jaya-prime/kandela-de-esperanza)), and shows up on Argentina and German radio stations even right now. The song "No ID" has easily been our second-most requested song to play live -- second only to "Arise" and "Come One, Come All", which are tied. God, I wish I had a recording of Jaime playing "Midliminal Gearchange" live. He might ditch on most guitarists, but damn he can make those strings sing!

The art came from my photo of one of the two fire pits at Indian Summer hookah bar in Monterey, California. Stars shining amid the coals of a fire pit is a warmth I would wish on everyone. I hear Indian Summer even survived the pandemic, but I haven't been back yet.  Not yet. Indian Summer even makes an appearance in my "[Landlore](landlore)" travel book. I really do need to get back there.

We are all just the volcanic ash of the sun that erupted out to form this spattering of planets that we now call a solar system.

In the three-years between my first album and this EP, I learned by leaps and bounds how to synthesize different instruments. I also grew more towards the electro genre and Japanese drum sets. I needed a way to connect what came before to what would follow next in the IO series... and I believe I achieved that.

Listen to and/or download the EP [here on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/the-ash-of-a-thousand-suns).

**Note**: With "No ID" being one of my more remixed songs and a fan favorite, I always keep samples for it on my MPC and there are more than 100 cuts of it at this point. The song has developed into four distinct paths that "most of the time" it follows: the dark carnival, alien abduction, cops n robbers, then finally murderbot which we've even done live. Tune into "[Warriors in Waiting](warriors-in-waiting-live-set)" for _that_ one. If you're a fan of the noid and haven't heard any of these, then here's a treat to tune into:
